CHIEF COMPLAINT
Rash evaluation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports her rash has improved significantly. She initially took doxycycline twice daily and noticed substantial improvement over two weeks. She then reduced to once daily last week on pharmacist recommendation when she perceived improvement. Since reducing to once daily, the improvement has plateaued. She continues sulfacetamide wash twice daily and metro cream applied after face wash. She did not use elidel due to concerns after reading about it. Physician clarified that risks associated with elidel apply to high-dose oral long-term use in transplant patients, not topical cream or ointment form for as-needed use. She attempted to obtain elidel but insurance does not cover it and GoodRx pricing was approximately $850. Tacrolimus ointment is being considered as alternative. Patient is not currently breastfeeding and stopped breastfeeding prior to initiating doxycycline. She reports sun sensitivity when outdoors and takes precautions including hat wearing. Physical examination reveals Fitzpatrick skin type IV with a few faint erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks and mild erythema around and underneath the nostrils.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient is not currently breastfeeding. Reports sun sensitivity when going outdoors and takes precautions including hat wearing.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Doxycycline
Sulfacetamide wash
Metro cream
Clindamycin (to be discontinued)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is not currently breastfeeding. Takes sun protection measures including wearing a hat when outdoors.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Skin: Fitzpatrick type IV; faint erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks; mild erythema around and underneath nostrils; no noted dryness or skin thinning

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis and rosacea including ocular rosacea.

1. Doxycycline: Increase to twice daily until rash resolves, then continue once daily for one additional week before discontinuing
2. Sulfacetamide wash: Continue
3. Metro cream: Continue after face wash
4. Tacrolimus ointment: Initiate twice daily, apply to rash area only, continue until rash resolved
5. Clindamycin: Remove from medication list
6. Elidel cream: Cancel from list
7. Moisturizer: Start vanicream or petroleum jelly; samples provided
8. Gently wash eyelids once daily with gentle cleanser such as vanicream; use Bruder mask as needed
9. Patient counseled on tacrolimus as calcineurin inhibitor, not a steroid; counseled that possible tingly or needle-like sensation or flushing 5-10 minutes after application lasts only seconds
10. Counseled to avoid steroids on face as they worsen rash and cause skin thinning
11. Counseled on doxycycline being low risk but noting potential for upset stomach, heartburn, and sun sensitivity requiring protection
12. Advised to avoid anti-aging products and plant-based products
13. Advised to discuss any new products with provider before use
14. Follow-up in approximately four weeks
15. If rash worsens, contact provider or send MyChart message; if rash recurs after resolution, may try tacrolimus alone for couple days, then restart doxycycline if needed
